name: Green River (Flaming Geyser)
blurb: Short, easy summer float out of Flaming Geyser State Park below the gorge.

sections.notes: Short, but an AW trip report took ~3 hr with a regular portage around a strainer about halfway. Scout for wood. Flaming Geyser State Park requires a Discover Pass. No fee or hours found for King County's Whitney Bridge Park.

notices.title: Check park gates and river-access signs
notices.text: State Parks lists these day-use areas open for winter 2026–27, with possible temporary weather closures. Hand-launch sites and the actual shore entry may differ from the Area marker. Check current park alerts before setting your shuttle.

putInAccess.sourceName: Washington State Parks — Flaming Geyser State Park
putInAccess.note: The current State Parks page and brochure describe kayaking on the park’s Green River frontage. The candidate matches the eastern picnic-area parking loop, shelters and lodge on the agency brochure and individual imagery, about 100 m inland. Several shoreline entries exist, and none is promoted as an exact landing. The 2026–27 schedule lists day use open but warns of periodic winter closures. This does not assert a developed boat ramp.
putInAccess.directions: Use the signed Flaming Geyser State Park entrance and the eastern day-use picnic area near the lodge. Carry boats using an open permitted river-access path and identify your shoreline entry or exit during the shuttle. Discover Pass required; respect gate hours and posted closures.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: King County Parks facility points (PARK_FACILITY_POINT_231), 'Boat Put-in Area (Non-motorized)' at Whitney Bridge Park (OBJECTID 327; owner, manager and maintainer King County Parks and Recreation)
takeOutAccess.note: Batch 3. Coordinate is King County Parks' own designated non-motorized boat put-in feature, 32 m from the v1/AW candidate. Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25, research/raw/batch3/whitney.png) puts it on the north bank just upstream (west) of the SE Green Valley Rd/212th Way SE bridge, about 10 m from the water through the bank vegetation. King County's same layer also has a 'Boat Launch Trailer Ramp' (OBJECTID 326; 47.282577, -122.054189) just downstream of the bridge, about 15 m from the water, as an alternative. Legal access: King County owns and manages Whitney Bridge Park (county GIS) and lists it among its parks (SE Green Valley Rd and 218th Ave SE, Auburn); King County Code 7.12.205.E permits boat launching in designated and posted areas, which this feature is. No fee or hours found on a county page (needs agency answer if hours matter).
takeOutAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
takeOutAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~289), the put-in area is on the north bank, right of the NHD centreline (~47 m; artificial path). Matches AW's 'take out on river right at Whitney Bridge'. Confirmed on imagery.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.
